doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Online music and club videos
summary: Segal wonders how musicians earn money with free music and is surprised the club is on YouTube.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Because everything’s free, you can get it online. I don’t know how the musicians make any money on that.
Yeah, I don’t either. I was just looking at YouTube this morning, just seeing some of the postings on there from the Jazz Showcase, and it goes back to...
Why? I don’t want it on there.
At the Blackstone I saw the Art Ensemble, 1981, Art Ensemble of Chicago. That’s...
Oh, that was released commercially. That was ok, yeah.
And then there’s a lot more that’s available from here that I’ve saw.
From this venue here, yeah. So it’s, you know... and there’s anywhere from - it looks like a lot of local musicians, some national acts there, but mostly local musicians.
Well some of them when they come in, they get their own people to take videos and they want to... Ow! Oof.
Phew! Just gotta stretch it a little.
We’re pretty close to wrapping up here, and then we’ll kind of jump around.
